L0@P0: Jan 2025
L1@P0:  Canine Liver Tumors
L2@P0: NC State University is enrolling dogs with liver tumors in a clinical trial
L3@P0: investigating a new therapy called INSPIRE, which uses electrical pulses to safely destroy the
L4@P0: membranes of cells within a tumor.
L5@P0: PARTICIPATION – Potential candidates will need to come in for a screening appointment at NC
L6@P0: State Veterinary Hospital to determine eligibility. If the patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial,
L7@P0: they will return 1-2 weeks for their first INSPIRE therapy treatment.
L8@P0: Eligible patients will fall into one of two categories. The first category patients will receive a liver
L9@P0: lobectomy a week after the INSPIRE treatment if the tumors are eligible for surgical resection. If the
L10@P0: tumors are not eligible for surgical resection the patient will fall into the second category where we
L11@P0: treat the tumors with the INSPIRE therapy up to 3 times at 3-week intervals. We will then monitor the
L12@P0: tumor over a 9-month period after their last INSPIRE treatment with 5 follow up visits that include a
L13@P0: CT scan and bloodwork.
L14@P0: INCLUSION CRITERIA – In order to participate in this study dogs must:
L15@P0: • Have 1-2 liver tumors measuring between 1-8 cm
L16@P0: • No other contraindicating comorbidities
L17@P0: • Patients must be ≥ 30lbs.
L18@P0: STUDY BENEFITS – FULLY FUNDED. Patients will receive an oncology consultation,
L19@P0: bloodwork at each study visit, multiple CT scans, echocardiogram with EKG, fine needle
L20@P0: aspirate with pathology report of liver tumor, +/- liver lobectomy.

L20: ## Kv9 Pilot Study
L21: 
L22: Purpose of study:
L23: 
L24: To assess efficacy and safety of Kv9 across a range of solid tumours.
L25: 
L26: ​
L27: 
L28: Eligible tumour types:
L29: 
L30:   * Soft tissue sarcomas
L31: 
L32:   * Mast cell tumours
L33: 
L34:   * Mammary gland tumours
L35: 
L36:   * Melanomas
L37: 
L38:   * Anal gland tumours
L39: 
L40:   * Squamous cell carcinomas
L41: 
L42:   * Other tumours may be considered
L43: 
L44: ​
L45: 
L46: Primary eligibility criteria*: ​
L47: 
L48:   * Tumour type diagnosed by fine needle aspirate or biopsy by a registered veterinary pathologist
L49: 
L50:   * ​Tumour smaller than 5cm
L51:   * Not receiving immune modulatory drugs
L52: 
L53:     * It is acceptable to be taking/receiving including apoquel, cytopoint, beranza or a recent vaccination
L54: 
L55:   * No wounds on the surface of soft tissue sarcoma tumours
L56: 
L57:     * Other tumour types will be a case by case basis ​
L58: 
L59: *See referral form for complete criteria ​
L60: 
L61: ​​​
L62: 
L63: Study protocol:
L64: 
L65:   1. Primary veterinarian to send through referral for assessment by Kode Veterinary Sciences (KVS).
L66: 
L67:   2. Additional testing completed as required.
L68:   3. Atleast two treatment appointments to receive Kv9 at treatment centres.
L69: 
L70:   4. A minimum of 9 revisits at primary care veterinarian or treatment centres over 2 years.
L71: 
L72: ​
L73: 
L74: Owner responsibilities:
L75: 
L76:   * You are responsible to schedule and attend all required visits  ​
L77: 
L78:   * You are responsible for the initial costs to diagnose your dogs tumour, and any other tests recommended by your veterinarian
L79:   * You are responsible to closely monitor your pet for any changes and update the clinical study team in a timely manner
L80: 
L81: ​
L82: 
L83: Financial support:
L84: 
L85:   * There is no cost to participate in the clinical study. KVS will cover the cost of treatment and monitoring appointments, and provide the Kv9 treatment free of charge.
L86:   * KVS will provide support to any participant experiencing adverse events during their time in the trial. If the event is suspected to be related to the Kv9 treatment, KVS will provide financial support, unless agreed to be excluded in the consent form.

L27: # Immunotherapy for canine oral melanoma
L28: 
L29: Oral melanoma is a highly aggressive disease with poor outcomes and no effective treatments. Our recent research has shown that a weakened form of the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is safe, and can trigger strong anti-tumor effects.
L30: By injecting a small amount of this weakened virus directly into the tumor, we aim to activate the dog's immune system to fight the cancer. Additionally, we will collect and expand immune cells from the tumor, as these cells are more likely to recognize and attack cancer cells. These enhanced immune cells will then be reinfused into the patient to target existing or potential metastatic disease.
L31: To evaluate our therapy, we will first perform a tumor biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and analyze the immune cells already present (Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes). We will then inject the tumor with the weakened virus. One week later, the tumor will be surgically removed, and immune cells from the cancer will be expanded for future use if metastases are present or develop later. After treatment, we will closely monitor the patients through periodic blood tests and imaging (CT scans) every three months.
L32: A small group of dogs (randomly selected) will be the control, and while not receiving the virus injection, they will have their immune cells extracted from the tumor and expanded to be reinfused in case of progressive disease.
L33: 
L34: 【8†Image: Image of Golden Retriever】
L35: #### Client Compensation:
L36: 
L37: Cost of tumor biopsy, two CT imaging sessions, trial-related blood work, the viral reagent and injections, the collection priming and reinjection of the immune cells. Additionally, participating dogs are eligible to receive a $800 post-trial incentive.
L38: 
L39: #### Potential Medical Benefits:
L40: 
L41: Potential medical benefits include longer clinical remissions after surgical removal of the primary tumor, slowing down or remission of metastatic disease.
L42: #### Potential Medical Risks:
L43: 
L44: Following tumor biopsy: bleeding, infection of the tumor, swelling, redness, pain, fever, and/or discharge/pus/odor at the biopsy site.
L45: Following virus injection and reinfusion of immune cells, skin rash, fever, lethargy, and anaphylaxis.
L46: #### What qualifies my pet for enrollment?
L47: 
L48: Inclusion Criteria:
L49: Dogs that are otherwise healthy with localized cytologically or histologically confirmed oral melanoma will be recruited to the study.
L50: 
L51: Tumors need to be easily accessible to percutaneous injection and needle biopsy.
L52: 
L53: Exclusion Criteria:
L54: Dogs with a history of immune deficiency or requiring immunosuppressive medications will be excluded.
L55: A dog that received local radiation therapy to the primary tumor before trial enrolment will be excluded.
L56: #### Diagnosis/Condition Being Studied:
L57: 
L58: Oral melanoma
L59: 
L60: ####
L61: Intervention to Be Studied:
L62: 
L63: Injection of weakened virus into the tumor and transfusion of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes

L27: # Use of AI-enhanced patient-specific biomechanical modeling to identify dogs with appendicular osteosarcoma undergoing stereotactic body radiation therapy who would benefit from minimally-invasive intramedullary stabilization
L28: The aim of this study is to perform initial testing for stabilization of long bones affected by osteosarcoma using a minimally-invasive implant with FDA approval for use in humans.  A previous study performed by the OSU-VMC determined that this implant was safe and well-tolerated in dogs.
L29:  The current study uses artificial-intelligence (AI)-enhanced, patient-specific biomechanical modeling to identify dogs at higher risk of experiencing a fracture from their tumor and determines whether they would benefit from receiving the implant.  Ultimately, the idea is that this minimally-invasive technology could be used to prevent pathologic fractures for dogs who undergo stereotactic body radiation therapy for osteosarcoma.
L30: Each dog will receive a CT scan for radiation therapy planning, followed by 3 treatments of radiation therapy to the tumor.  The CT scan will also be used to assess the risk of fracture and determine whether the dog would benefit from placement of the implant.
L31:  If determined that the dog’s fracture risk would be improved by placement of the implant, following completion of radiation therapy, the dog will be placed under general anesthesia the day after the final radiation therapy treatment for implantation of the device.  Dogs enrolled in this trial will undergo chemotherapy treatment with carboplatin, an intravenous chemotherapy, for up to 6 treatments following completion of stereotactic body radiation therapy.
L32: Gait analysis will be performed at enrollment and at the 2 week recheck examination, followed by every 2 months, along with chest x-rays to monitor for spread of disease.
L33: 【8†Image: Older black and brown dog laying on a dog bed.】
L34: #### Client Compensation:
L35: The costs of the following will be covered as part of the study: pre-operative limb CT, pre-operative initial gait evaluation, anesthesia for implant placement, implant and implant application, intra-operative fluoroscopy, histopathology, and post-operative limb radiographs.  The study will also cover the cost of follow-up limb radiographs and gait evaluations.
L36:  In addition, at the conclusion of participation in the study, you will be provided with a $1000 direct payment to help cover other costs associated with treatment of the osteosarcoma.  This study does not cover the cost of stereotactic body radiation therapy or chemotherapy.
L37: ####
L38: Potential Medical Benefits:
L39: 
L40: Dogs participating in this study may avoid developing pathologic fractures of the limb affected with osteosarcoma.  The goal is to determine whether the AI-enhanced modeling and application of the implant to patients at risk of fracturing can prevent the development of fractures.
L41: #### Potential Medical Risks:
L42: There are some risks associated with anesthesia and surgery that will be explained by the primary clinician and detailed on the consent form for the procedure.  There are some risks associated with radiation therapy that will be explained by the primary clinician.  The risks associated with the implant include implant failure, infection, pathologic fracture, and tumor recurrence.  It is possible that dogs in this study may experience unexpected side effects resulting from anesthesia or surgery.
L43:  It is possible that the dog’s condition may not improve or may worsen.  The dogs will be observed closely for side effects and appropriate medical care will be provided.

L27: # Targeting MIC to Augment Adoptive NK Therapy Using the Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma Model
L28: 
L29: The trial will examine the use of a new canine antibody that will improve the activation of immune cells to target the cancer.
L30: Dogs enrolled in the trial will have procedures that include blood draws, diagnostic imaging (CT, chest radiograph, ultrasound), tumor biopsy, injection of antibodies, and infusion of immune cells.
L31: 
L32: 【8†Image: decorative photo of dog.】
L33: #### Client Compensation:
L34: 
L35: Once enrolled, all trial-related procedures will be covered in addition to $700 upon completion of the trial.
L36: 
L37: #### Potential Medical Benefits:
L38: 
L39: This study examines new therapeutic approach for soft tissue sarcomas that use the immune system to attack the cancer. Your dog might benefit from this new therapy that is aimed to control the local and metastatic disease and prolong life.
L40: #### Potential Medical Risks:
L41: 
L42: The risk of adverse effects with the therapies in this trial is low but still possible.  Injection of the anti-MIC antibody and NK cells may cause infection, anaphylactic shock, collapse, anorexia, vomiting, diarrhea, and, in extreme situations, even death. It is possible that your dog's condition may not improve, or it may worsen or even die. Your dog will be observed closely for side effects, and appropriate medical care will be provided if needed.
L43: #### What qualifies my pet for enrollment?
L44: 
L45: Inclusion Criteria:
L46: The following dogs may be included in the Trial:
L47: •    Dogs that are otherwise healthy with localized cytologically or histologically confirmed soft tissue sarcoma will be recruited to the trial.
L48: Exclusion Criteria:
L49: The following dogs will be excluded from the trial:
L50: •    Dogs with a history of immune deficiency or requiring immunosuppressive medications will be excluded.
L51: •    Dogs received local radiation therapy to the primary tumor before the study intervention.
L52: 
L53: Diagnosis/Condition Being Studied:
L54: Canine Soft Tissue Sarcomas
L55: 
L56: Intervention to Be Studied:
L57: Injection of MIC antibody and infusion of immune cells (Natural killer cells expanded from the tumor and reinjected to patient)
